R01.note: Explains the lost mitigation with measured timings and their limits, corrects the earlier recommendation, and avoids inventing unavailable code snippets.

errors: "the one real downside is small" is not established by the incident-free period.
"it takes effect in about a minute" turns historical time to mitigate into a measured flag propagation time.
"a checkout outage would last about 12 minutes instead of 1" excludes detection and preparation time and assumes either intervention resolves the future incident.
R02.note: Makes the cleanup scope clear but presents deployment duration as a guaranteed future outage duration.

errors: "if the new checkout breaks you flip the flag off ... in ~1 minute" assumes the historical mitigation will work for a future failure.
"a fix needs a revert + deploy" presents one possible recovery procedure as necessary.
R03.note: Answers the downside compactly, but omits the issue's actual two-week rule and overgeneralizes the historical recovery.

errors: "roughly 11 extra minutes of live breakage" is not established by comparing historical mitigation time with merge-to-live deployment time.
"there's no way to disable the new checkout at all" is unsupported; other operational controls were not investigated.
"Everything else is in favor of deleting" claims completeness beyond the supplied evidence.
"a flag that will otherwise live forever" is unsupported.
"the 3-week window proves the new flow survives normal traffic" overstates what an incident-free record proves.
"the revert of that merge serves the same purpose at the same ~12-minute cost as any other fix" assumes preparation time and effectiveness are equivalent.
R04.note: Names the recovery tradeoff but repeatedly converts limited measurements into absolute claims.

errors: "today a broken new checkout can be switched off in about a minute" assumes the fallback still works and resolves the future failure.
"Checkout stays broken until that deploy lands" assumes no other mitigation and a continuous failure.
"a possible 11-minute-longer outage" is an incomplete estimate because restoration preparation time is unknown.
R05.note: Gives a useful sequence and explicitly includes preparation time, but repeats the argument and partially undermines its own uncertainty about the fallback.

errors: "I have no concrete reason not to delete it" disregards the concrete lost mitigation option described immediately afterward.
"currently takes about 1 minute to mitigate a checkout incident" treats two historical results as a current general guarantee.
"mitigating an incident requires reverting the code" is unsupported as a universal recovery requirement.
"the 40-second CI cost ... outweighs the lost 1-minute toggle mitigation" is a judgment presented as following necessarily from the stability threshold.
R06.note: Introduces the relevant files and cleanup rule clearly, but its opening denies the downside its own explanation identifies.

errors: "a code rollback would take about 12 minutes to reach production" substitutes deployment duration for total rollback duration.
R07.note: Directly answers the question with little waste, but leaves the removal threshold and recovery timing limitations unstated.

errors: "wastes ~40 seconds" assumes the fallback tests provide no useful value.
"riskier than relying on the 12-minute deploy for a forward fix" has no supporting comparison of failure likelihood or recovery effectiveness.
"unexercised code" ignores the 31 legacy-path tests unless explicitly limited to recent production traffic.
R08.note: Answers the costs of keeping the flag instead of the requested costs of deleting it, and invents a comparative risk assessment.

errors: "about 13 minutes to undo instead of 1" invents a restoration preparation duration.
"the only way back to the old checkout" is unsupported; code restoration is itself another way.
"checkout stays broken for roughly 13 minutes" assumes both an unverified duration and continuous failure until recovery.
"the only evidence that the flag has ever been needed" exceeds the supplied incident history.
"If a big peak is coming ... that is a reason to wait for it" adds an unsupported exception to the agreed cleanup condition.
R09.note: Provides context and a sequence, but its central thirteen-minute estimate is invented and repeated as evidence.

errors: "if checkout breaks ... it's fixed in about 1 minute" guarantees future mitigation from historical incidents.
"A checkout outage would last roughly 12 times longer" compares unlike timing measurements and assumes both recovery methods succeed.
"every future checkout change has to consider" the flag is broader than the verified facts.
"the flag check in src/flags.ts" invents the location of the checkout branching logic; only the flag's location was verified.
"wait until after your next high-traffic period" introduces an additional safeguard without evidence that this period changes the decision.
R10.note: Offers an actionable cleanup scope, but exaggerates the timing comparison and invents where the flag check lives.

errors: "mitigation goes from about 1 minute to about 12" treats deployment duration as total future mitigation time.
"The only mitigation left is code" excludes uninvestigated operational alternatives.
"Checkout is broken for every user" inflates a hypothetical payment failure into a universal outage.
"about 11 minutes of reduced exposure per checkout incident" assumes every incident can be mitigated by the flag and both historical timings generalize.
"both in the rollout month, while it was actively moving traffic" contradicts the supplied timing of incidents in the month before rollout and invents rollout activity.
"The flag branch in src/flags.ts" invents the location of the checkout branching logic.
"my only evidence is the 31 tests" implies evidence of fallback functionality without verified test results.
R11.note: Explains many names, but buries the answer in repetition while adding unsupported incident history and universal failure claims.

errors: "the only code reachable in the off position" reverses the verified condition: the legacy path is reachable only when off, not necessarily the only reachable code.
"the two entries ... list a flag flip" invents details of the incident log's contents beyond the supplied summary.
"~12 minutes instead of ~1 minute" omits preparation time from the future recovery comparison.
"waiting longer ... only keeps charging the test and review cost" invents a measured review cost and excludes the possible value of additional production observation.
"I have no concrete reason to wait" overlooks the lost fast fallback that the reply subsequently describes.
R12.note: Marks the future timing comparison as an inference, but excessive definitions and repetition obscure the answer and its deciding rule.
